correctness.rationale: After dilation the window is a fixed Gaussian derivative with stable integer shifts, because the periodized squared Fourier modulus is continuous and cannot vanish at every integer translate. The non-frame criterion therefore produces a bounded-coefficient Gaussian shift-invariant entire function whose \(m\)-th derivative vanishes on the lattice. For \(N>m\), differentiating the Wronskian fewer than \(N-m\) times yields generalized row orders whose sum is too small to avoid the row order \(m\); hence each common \(m\)-th derivative zero has Wronskian multiplicity at least \(N-m\). Faulhuber--Petersen's translate-independence, automorphy, and Gaussian zero-density steps then give \((N-m)/(N\delta)\le1\). Arbitrarily large \(N\) are allowed for irrational \(\delta\), while for \(p/q\) one takes \(N=q\), yielding exactly \(q-p\le m\).
residual_risks: No correctness defect was found; the result is one-sided for higher derivative order.

value.rationale: This is a structural extension of a newly introduced Wronskian-amplification method: it turns the exact first-derivative obstruction into an all-order irrational-safety theorem and a clean rational deficit barrier. The higher-order multiplicity lemma is independently reusable and the statement addresses a natural frame-set boundary rather than a finite experiment.
residual_risks: It deliberately stops short of a full higher-order frame-set classification.

final_claim: For the \(m\)-th derivative of a Gaussian, every rectangular Gabor lattice with irrational product \(0<\delta<1\) is a frame, while a reduced rational product \(\delta=p/q<1\) can fail only if \(q-p\le m\).
limitations: For \(m\ge2\) the remaining rational products with \(q-p\le m\) are not classified.
The result concerns derivatives of one fixed Gaussian scale and rectangular lattices, not arbitrary polynomial-times-Gaussian windows or the standard higher Hermite functions.
